source_text.body:
Run personal assistant, content and brand-deal bots
The author built three Grok Bot agents: one as personal assistant, one repurposing newsletters and replying to YouTube comments, and one handling brand deals including an NDA.
Done with
GB
Grok Bot
What they did
Remy Gaskell created three Grok Bot agents by filling out a questionnaire: Alfred (personal assistant), Gordon (content), and Florence (brand deals). Each has its own cloud computer, and his existing skills library imported in one click. Gordon repurposed last week's newsletter for X and LinkedIn and began replying to YouTube comments. Asked to sign an NDA, Alfred messaged Florence and handed the task to her.
How it went
Gordon's outputs were solid with almost no training, and he now works automatically. Gordon spent an hour failing to post an article to X, and Remy couldn't inspect, understand or stop it.
Worth knowing
Grok Bot comes with qualifying plans such as the $200/month Cursor Ultra tier. A stuck agent keeps using your allowance, and the interface gives you few ways to step in.
Try it yourself
with
Grok Bot
Copy prompt
Act as my assistant for [my work, e.g. newsletter and YouTube channel]. Each [day or week], take my latest [newsletter issue] and turn it into [format, e.g. 3 social posts and a short video script], and draft replies to new comments on [channel or platform] in my voice, which is [tone description]. Done means a single list of drafts for me to review, nothing posted. Before posting, replying, sending any message or signing anything, show me the exact text and wait for my approval.
Original source: https://www.aiwithremy.com/posts/what-i-m-actually-using-grok-bot-for
